_meta.source: resources/Vann Brothers test cases/Vann Brothers test cases/AgriFarm_VannBrothers_Regression_Suite_Web_iOS.xlsx
_meta.note: Regenerate with `pnpm catalog`. Execution status is not carried here.

cases.prerequisite: Valid AgriERP QA credentials (Azure AD / f3dynamics.onmicrosoft.com)
cases.title: Verify login to the AgriFarm web app with valid credentials
cases.steps:
1. Open https://agrierp-vann-qa.folio3.site
2. Enter a valid username and password
3. Complete MFA if prompted
cases.expected: The identity provider authenticates the user, the app lands on the default module, and the header shows the user's Grower, Site and Season.

cases.title: Verify login is rejected with an invalid password
cases.steps:
1. Enter a valid username with an incorrect password
2. Submit
cases.expected: Login fails with a clear error from the identity provider; no partial session is created and the user is not routed into the app shell.

cases.title: Verify unauthenticated deep-link access is blocked
cases.steps: 1. In a fresh/incognito browser open https://agrierp-vann-qa.folio3.site/workorders directly
cases.expected: User is redirected to the sign-in page; after successful sign-in the originally requested route is restored.

cases.title: Verify Log Out terminates the session
cases.steps:
1. Click the avatar (top-right)
2. Click 'Log Out'
3. After redirect press browser Back
cases.expected: Session is terminated, the sign-in page is shown, and Back does not restore any authenticated page or cached data.

cases.title: Verify session expiry / silent token refresh behaviour
cases.steps:
1. Log in and leave the app idle beyond the configured token lifetime
2. Return and click any module
cases.expected: Either the token refreshes silently and the action succeeds, or the user is cleanly redirected to sign-in. The app never shows a blank screen or an unhandled 401.

cases.prerequisite: Account exists in D365 but not provisioned in AgriERP
cases.title: Verify an unprovisioned but authenticated account is handled
cases.steps:
1. Authenticate with an account that has no AgriERP user record
2. Observe the landing behaviour
cases.expected: A clear 'no access / not provisioned' message is shown. The user is not dropped into an empty shell with broken module calls.

cases.prerequisite: A user set to Inactive in Settings > User Management
cases.title: Verify an inactive user cannot access the application
cases.steps:
1. Deactivate a user via Settings > Users
2. Attempt to sign in as that user
cases.expected: Sign-in is blocked with an explicit message stating the account is inactive; any pre-existing session for that user is invalidated on next request.

cases.prerequisite: AgriERP iOS build installed on iPhone/iPad, valid credentials
cases.title: Verify login to the iOS app with valid credentials
cases.steps:
1. Launch the AgriERP app
2. Enter valid credentials on the login screen
3. Complete MFA if prompted
cases.expected: The user is authenticated, the dashboard tiles render, and the profile shows the correct Grower, Location and Season.

cases.title: Verify login is rejected with invalid credentials on iOS
cases.steps:
1. Enter an incorrect password and submit
2. Repeat with a non-existent username
cases.expected: Both attempts fail with a readable in-app error; the app does not crash, hang on a spinner, or cache the failed credentials.

cases.title: Verify the iOS session persists across an app restart
cases.steps:
1. Log in
2. Force-quit the app from the app switcher
3. Relaunch
cases.expected: The user remains signed in and lands on the dashboard without re-entering credentials, provided the token is still valid.

cases.title: Verify Log Out on iOS clears local data
cases.steps:
1. Log out from the app menu
2. Relaunch the app
3. Attempt to open a previously cached work order offline
cases.expected: Login screen is shown, no cached work-order data is reachable without authenticating, and the local store is cleared per the security policy.

cases.title: Verify concurrent sessions on web and iOS are supported
cases.steps:
1. Log in on web and on the iOS app with the same account
2. Perform an action on each
cases.expected: Both sessions remain valid and functional; actions on one platform do not silently invalidate the other unless single-session policy is configured.

cases.title: Verify all primary modules are present in the header
cases.steps: 1. Observe the header navigation bar
cases.expected: Header shows Maps, Planning, Work Orders, Harvest Central, Template Management and Communication Center, with no missing or duplicated entries.

cases.title: Verify each header module link routes to the correct page
cases.steps:
1. Click Maps, Planning, Work Orders, Harvest Central, Template Management and Communication Center in turn
2. Check the URL each time
cases.expected: Routes resolve to /maps, /crop-mgmt, /workorders, /harvest-central, /template-mgmt and /messaging respectively, each rendering its own page without error.

cases.title: Verify the active module is visually highlighted
cases.steps:
1. Navigate to each module in turn
2. Observe nav item styling
cases.expected: The nav item for the open module is highlighted; all others are in the default state. The highlight survives an in-module navigation and a page refresh.

cases.title: Verify the breadcrumb reflects the current location and is navigable
cases.steps:
1. Open Template Management > Inspection Template > Create
2. Click each breadcrumb node in turn
cases.expected: Breadcrumb shows the full path, each node navigates to the correct ancestor page, and the trailing node is not clickable.

cases.prerequisite: User mapped to more than one grower
cases.title: Verify the Grower dropdown lists only growers the user is mapped to
cases.steps: 1. Open the Grower selector in the header/profile
cases.expected: Only growers the signed-in user is mapped to are listed. Growers outside the mapping are absent, including from the type-ahead results.

cases.title: Verify changing the Grower re-filters the Location list
cases.steps:
1. Select Grower A and note the locations offered
2. Switch to Grower B
3. Reopen the Location list
cases.expected: The Location list refreshes immediately to show only locations mapped to the newly selected grower; no Grower A locations remain selectable.

cases.prerequisite: Grower with no locations mapped to the user
cases.title: Verify a grower with no accessible locations is handled
cases.steps: 1. Select a grower for which the user holds no location rights
cases.expected: A clear 'No locations available' state is shown; module pages either stay on a safe empty state or prompt for a valid selection rather than erroring.

cases.title: Verify grower selection persists after re-login
cases.steps:
1. Select a non-default grower
2. Log out and log back in
cases.expected: The previously selected grower is restored (or the configured default is applied consistently) rather than resetting unpredictably.

cases.prerequisite: User with access to more than one site
cases.title: Verify the Site dropdown lists all permitted sites with search
cases.steps:
1. Click 'Site: <current>' in the header
2. Type part of a site name
cases.expected: Dropdown lists the permitted sites (e.g. Yolo, Colusa); the type-ahead filters correctly and clearing it restores the full list.

cases.title: Verify switching site reloads module data for the new site
cases.steps:
1. Note the field count on Maps for the current site
2. Switch Site
3. Observe the Maps sidebar and extent
cases.expected: Header label, sidebar tree, counters and map extent all reload for the new site with no data from the previous site remaining on screen.

cases.prerequisite: Work Orders list open with a filter applied
cases.title: Verify site switch is honoured on a data grid
cases.steps:
1. Open Work Orders and apply a status filter
2. Switch Site
3. Observe the grid
cases.expected: The grid reloads scoped to the new site; the applied filter behaves per design (retained or cleared) and no cross-site rows leak into the results.

cases.title: Verify the Season dropdown lists available crop years
cases.steps: 1. Click 'Season: <current>' in the header
cases.expected: Dropdown lists the configured crop years (e.g. Crop Year 2025 and Crop Year 2026) and marks the currently selected one.

cases.title: Verify switching season refreshes season-scoped data
cases.steps:
1. Note the ticket counts on Harvest Central
2. Switch Season
3. Observe the list
cases.expected: Header label and all season-scoped datasets refresh to the newly selected crop year; counts change accordingly with no cross-season leakage.

cases.title: Verify season selection persists across navigation and refresh
cases.steps:
1. Switch Season
2. Navigate Maps > Planning > Work Orders
3. Refresh the browser (F5)
cases.expected: The selected season is retained on every module and survives the refresh.

cases.prerequisite: On Maps with a site selected
cases.title: Verify the weather widget displays current conditions
cases.steps: 1. Click the weather icon / 'See Weather Details' in the header
cases.expected: A panel shows temperature, condition text, humidity, wind and any forecast rows, for the location of the selected site.

cases.title: Verify weather values are plausible and unit-labelled
cases.steps:
1. Open the weather panel and inspect each value
2. Cross-check against a public weather source for the same location
cases.expected: Temperature carries an explicit unit, percentages are within 0-100, wind has a unit and direction, and values are within a plausible range of the reference source.

cases.title: Verify the Dynamics 365 F&O shortcut opens the correct environment
cases.steps: 1. Click the 'Navigate to Microsoft Dynamics 365 F&O' icon
cases.expected: The D365 F&O QA environment opens in a new browser tab. A QA build must never link to the production D365 environment.

cases.title: Verify the notification bell opens the notification list
cases.steps: 1. Click the notification icon in the header
cases.expected: The panel opens listing recent notifications newest-first, each with a timestamp and a working link to the related record where applicable.

cases.prerequisite: An event that raises a notification (flagged message, WO assignment)
cases.title: Verify a new notification is raised and the unread badge updates
cases.steps:
1. Trigger a notifiable event from another account
2. Observe the bell without refreshing, then refresh
cases.expected: The unread count increases, the new item appears at the top of the list, and opening it clears the unread state.

cases.title: Verify user menu content is correct
cases.steps: 1. Click the avatar initials in the header
cases.expected: The menu shows display name/role, admin flag, User Settings, Sync Console (admins only), Grower, Help, Version, Environment and Log Out.

cases.title: Verify the displayed application version matches the deployed build
cases.steps:
1. Read the Version value
2. Compare with the release notes / build pipeline for the QA environment
cases.expected: The version string matches the build actually deployed to the environment under test.

cases.title: Verify the Environment label matches the environment under test
cases.steps: 1. Read the Environment value
cases.expected: It reads the QA environment name on the QA site. A production build must never display a QA label or vice versa.

cases.title: Verify the Help link opens the documentation location
cases.steps: 1. Click 'Help'
cases.expected: The configured help/documentation location opens in a new tab and is reachable by the tester's account (no 404 or auth wall).

cases.title: Verify Sync Console visibility is role-gated
cases.steps:
1. As an admin open the user menu and click 'Sync Console'
2. Repeat with a non-admin account, then deep-link directly to the Sync Console route
cases.expected: Admins reach the console; non-admins neither see the menu entry nor reach it by direct URL - they receive an access-denied response.

cases.title: Verify default page size and page-size switching
cases.steps:
1. Open a list page
2. Change the page-size selector to 20, 50 and 100 in turn
cases.expected: The grid reloads with the requested row count each time and the 'Showing X - Y of Z records' label stays accurate.

cases.title: Verify pagination navigation across first/prev/next/last
cases.steps: 1. Use next, previous, first and last controls in sequence
cases.expected: The correct page is rendered each time, no row is duplicated or skipped between pages, and the record label is accurate at every step.

cases.title: Verify per-column search filters the grid
cases.steps:
1. Click the column search icon
2. Enter a partial value in one column and apply
cases.expected: Only rows matching that value in that column remain; clearing the search restores the unfiltered grid.

cases.title: Verify multiple column searches combine with AND logic
cases.steps: 1. Apply a search on two different columns at once
cases.expected: Only rows satisfying both criteria are returned; removing one criterion widens the result set predictably.

cases.title: Verify column sorting including dates and numbers
cases.steps:
1. Click a sortable header once, then again
2. Repeat for a date column and a numeric column
cases.expected: Rows sort ascending then descending. Dates sort chronologically and numbers numerically - not as text strings.

cases.title: Verify the 'Refresh Data' control reloads the grid
cases.steps:
1. Click Refresh Data
2. Observe the loading state and the returned data
cases.expected: A loading indicator appears, a fresh request is issued, and records created elsewhere since page load now appear.

cases.title: Verify empty-state handling
cases.steps: 1. Search a column for a value that does not exist
cases.expected: A clear 'No records found' empty state is shown instead of a blank grid or an endless spinner, and the filter can be cleared from that state.

cases.title: Verify a failed API call does not strand the user on a dead-end screen
cases.steps:
1. Trigger a failing request (block the API in devtools or open a known failing tab)
2. Observe the page
cases.expected: An inline error or toast is shown with a retry path. The user retains working navigation and is not forced into a full page reload.

cases.title: Verify an unknown route renders the 404 page
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to https://agrierp-vann-qa.folio3.site/this-does-not-exist
cases.expected: The custom 404 page is shown with a working route back into the application; no raw framework error is exposed.

cases.title: Verify all visible labels are resolved translation strings
cases.steps:
1. Walk through every module, list and form
2. Look for raw resource keys or untranslated placeholders
cases.expected: No raw i18n keys, no 'undefined' labels and no empty tooltips are shown anywhere in the UI.

cases.prerequisite: A user with Default Language = Spanish
cases.title: Verify the language switch translates the UI
cases.steps:
1. Set Default Language to Spanish in User Settings
2. Reload and navigate every module
cases.expected: Labels, buttons, validation messages and grid headers render in the selected language; layout does not break on longer strings.

cases.title: Verify date and time rendering follows the configured format
cases.steps:
1. Inspect dates on Work Orders, Harvest Central and Sync History
2. Compare with the configured format and timezone
cases.expected: Dates render in the configured format consistently across modules, and times honour the user's timezone/12-24h preference.

cases.title: Verify role-based visibility and enforcement of actions
cases.steps:
1. Log in as a restricted role
2. Compare available actions (Create, Edit, Delete, Post Ticket, Sync Console) against an admin
3. Attempt a restricted action by direct URL or API call
cases.expected: Restricted actions are hidden in the UI and also rejected server-side when invoked directly - visibility alone is not the control.

cases.title: Verify the dashboard tiles render for the signed-in role
cases.steps:
1. Log in
2. Inspect the dashboard tiles
cases.expected: Tiles for Map, Work Orders, Inspection, Point of Interest and any other entitled modules render, and tiles the role has no rights to are absent.

cases.title: Verify Grower / Location / Season selection in the mobile profile
cases.steps:
1. Open the profile section
2. Change Grower, then Location, then Season
cases.expected: Each selector lists only entitled values, changing the grower re-filters the location list, and the selection is applied to the dashboard data.

cases.title: Verify the app version and environment shown in the mobile app
cases.steps: 1. Open the app menu / About screen
cases.expected: The build number matches the build under test and the environment label reads QA, not production.

cases.title: Verify first-run permission prompts are requested correctly
cases.steps:
1. Install a fresh build and launch
2. Observe the permission prompts for Location, Camera, Microphone, Photos and Notifications
cases.expected: Each permission is requested with a clear purpose string at the point it is needed, and denying one degrades only that feature rather than blocking the app.

cases.title: Verify graceful behaviour when Location permission is denied
cases.steps:
1. Deny Location permission
2. Open Map, then attempt to create an observation
cases.expected: The app explains that location is required, offers a route to iOS Settings, and does not crash or silently record a null coordinate.

cases.title: Verify pull-to-refresh on the dashboard and list screens
cases.steps:
1. Create a work order on web
2. On iOS pull down to refresh the relevant list
cases.expected: The list re-fetches from the server, the spinner terminates, and the new record appears.

cases.title: Verify app behaviour on background and resume
cases.steps:
1. Open a work order
2. Background the app for 5 minutes
3. Resume
cases.expected: The app resumes on the same screen with data intact, refreshes stale data where required, and does not force a re-login while the token is valid.

cases.prerequisite: Two iOS devices of different sizes (e.g. iPhone SE and iPhone Pro Max)
cases.title: Verify layout on small and large iPhone screens
cases.steps:
1. Run the core flows on both devices
2. Inspect headers, lists, forms and modals
cases.expected: No text truncation, overlap or off-screen controls on either device; tap targets remain reachable and scrollable areas scroll fully.

cases.title: Verify the app renders acceptably on iPad
cases.steps: 1. Install and run the core flows on iPad in portrait and landscape
cases.expected: The layout is usable at tablet size (scaled or adaptive per design), with no clipped controls and no broken map rendering.

cases.prerequisite: Latest and minimum supported iOS versions available
cases.title: Verify the app runs on the minimum supported iOS version
cases.steps:
1. Install on a device running the minimum supported iOS version
2. Execute the smoke path (login, map, start job, enter progress, end job)
cases.expected: All smoke steps complete without crash or visual defect on the minimum supported OS version.

cases.title: Verify Dynamic Type and dark mode do not break layouts
cases.steps:
1. Set a larger text size in iOS Settings and enable dark mode
2. Navigate the main screens
cases.expected: Text scales without clipping or overlap, contrast remains legible in dark mode, and no control becomes unreachable.

cases.prerequisite: Logged-in user, site and season selected
cases.title: Verify the Maps module loads the farm boundary and field polygons
cases.steps:
1. Click Maps in the header
2. Wait for the map to render
cases.expected: The map renders centred on the selected farm with all field polygons drawn and labelled; no console errors and no missing tiles.

cases.title: Verify farm summary counters are correct
cases.steps:
1. Open the Details aside > Summary tab
2. Compare with the sidebar tree
cases.expected: Farm Name, Location, No of Fields and Total Area are shown and reconcile exactly with the sidebar field list.

cases.prerequisite: A site or season with unmapped fields
cases.title: Verify empty/partial geometry handling
cases.steps: 1. Switch to a site or season containing fields with no boundary geometry
cases.expected: The map still renders; unmapped fields are omitted or clearly flagged; no JavaScript error and no infinite loading state.

cases.title: Verify map load time with the full QA dataset
cases.steps:
1. Hard-refresh Maps and measure time to first fully rendered polygon set
2. Repeat three times and take the median
cases.expected: The map reaches a usable rendered state within the agreed threshold; the measured value is recorded in Comments for trend tracking.

cases.title: Verify the Map / Satellite base-layer toggle
cases.steps:
1. Click 'Satellite'
2. Click 'Map'
cases.expected: The base layer switches between roadmap and satellite imagery; field polygons and labels stay aligned and visible in both.

cases.title: Verify the Terrain and Labels sub-options
cases.steps:
1. Hover the base-layer control
2. Toggle 'Terrain' and 'Labels'
cases.expected: Terrain shading and place labels are applied and removed without losing the field overlay.

cases.title: Verify zoom in / zoom out controls
cases.steps: 1. Click Zoom in three times, then Zoom out three times
cases.expected: The zoom level changes smoothly, polygons and labels rescale correctly, and the view returns to a comparable extent.

cases.title: Verify the fullscreen toggle
cases.steps:
1. Click 'Toggle fullscreen view'
2. Press Esc
cases.expected: The map expands to fullscreen and restores correctly; controls and the layer panel remain usable in both states.

cases.title: Verify pan and drag behaviour
cases.steps: 1. Click and drag the map in several directions
cases.expected: The map pans smoothly, tiles load progressively and field overlays stay aligned with the base imagery.

cases.title: Verify Street View (Pegman) behaves gracefully
cases.steps: 1. Drag Pegman onto a road near a field
cases.expected: Street View opens where imagery exists; where it does not, the control degrades gracefully without a broken panel.

cases.title: Verify the Maps Control panel lists all configured layers
cases.steps: 1. Click 'Maps Control'
cases.expected: The panel lists Stages, Crops, Task/Operation, Active/Draft/Completed Inspections, Upcoming/Active/Completed Work Orders, Observations and Point of Interest.

cases.title: Verify the Crops layer colour-codes fields by crop
cases.steps:
1. Select the Crops layer
2. Observe the map and legend
cases.expected: Fields are shaded by crop/variety with a legend matching the shading; field labels remain readable over the fill.

cases.title: Verify the Stages layer reflects each plot's current growth stage
cases.steps:
1. Select the Stages layer
2. Cross-check three plots against Planning
cases.expected: Fields are shaded by current stage and the shading matches the stage shown for the same plot in the Planning module.

cases.prerequisite: Work orders exist in several statuses
cases.title: Verify the Upcoming (To Do) work order layer
cases.steps:
1. Select the Upcoming Work Order layer
2. Cross-check against the Work Orders list filtered to 'To Do'
cases.expected: Only plots carrying To Do work orders are highlighted and the set matches the filtered work order list exactly.

cases.title: Verify the Active (In Progress) work order layer
cases.steps:
1. Select the Active Work Order layer
2. Cross-check against the Work Orders list filtered to 'In Progress'
cases.expected: Only plots carrying In Progress work orders are highlighted and the set matches the filtered list.

cases.prerequisite: Completed work orders exist, including some ended from the mobile app
cases.title: Verify the Completed work order layer includes mobile-completed work orders
cases.steps:
1. Complete a work order from the iOS app
2. Refresh Maps and select the Completed Work Order layer
cases.expected: The plot for the mobile-completed work order is highlighted under Completed. This has regressed previously (mobile completions missing from the completed list).

cases.title: Verify the Active / Draft / Completed Inspection layers
cases.steps:
1. Select each inspection layer in turn
2. Cross-check against Work Orders > Inspection Work Orders
cases.expected: Highlighted plots match the inspection work orders in the corresponding status for each layer.

cases.title: Verify the inspection flag/indicator renders on the map
cases.steps: 1. Select the Active Inspection layer, then the Completed Inspection layer
cases.expected: A flag or marker is drawn on each plot with an inspection in the selected status, distinguishable between active and completed.

cases.title: Verify the Observations layer
cases.steps:
1. Select the Observations layer
2. Click a highlighted plot
cases.expected: Plots with observations are marked and selecting one surfaces the related observation(s) with a route to the detail.

cases.prerequisite: POI types configured and observations captured
cases.title: Verify the Point of Interest layer renders configured pin icons and colours
cases.steps:
1. Select the Point of Interest layer
2. Compare pins against the POI configuration in Settings
cases.expected: Each pin uses the icon and colour configured for its POI category; disabled categories are not plotted.

cases.title: Verify switching layers clears the previous overlay
cases.steps: 1. Select 'Crops', then select 'Active Work Orders'
cases.expected: Only the newly selected layer's styling is applied; the previous layer's colours and markers are fully removed.

cases.title: Verify the Task/Operation layer groups plots by operation
cases.steps: 1. Select the Task/Operation layer
cases.expected: Plots are shaded by the operation associated with their current work, with a matching legend.

cases.prerequisite: Admin access to Settings > Map Toggle Configuration
cases.title: Verify colours configured in Map Toggle Config apply to the Upcoming WO layer
cases.steps:
1. Set a distinctive colour for Upcoming Work Orders in Map Toggle Configuration and save
2. Open Maps and select that layer
cases.expected: The plots render in exactly the configured colour; the legend swatch matches.

cases.title: Verify colours apply to Active and Completed Work Order layers
cases.steps:
1. Configure distinct colours for Active and Completed Work Orders
2. Verify each layer on the map
cases.expected: Both layers render in their configured colours with no colour bleeding between statuses.

cases.title: Verify colours apply to Crop, Stage and Operation layers
cases.steps:
1. Configure colours for a crop, a stage and an operation
2. Verify each layer on the map
cases.expected: Each layer honours its configured colour mapping and the legend agrees with the map fill.

cases.prerequisite: POI categories exist with pins already placed
cases.title: Verify changing a POI category colour does not retro-change existing pins
cases.steps:
1. Note the colour of existing pins for a POI category
2. Change the category colour in configuration
3. Return to the map
cases.expected: Behaviour matches the agreed rule (previously placed pins retain their original colour); any change is logged in the POI category change log.

cases.title: Verify configuration changes are saved and survive a reload
cases.steps:
1. Change several settings and save
2. Reload the page and reopen the configuration
cases.expected: All changes persist exactly as saved with a success confirmation on save.

cases.title: Verify the Advance Filter panel opens with all expected criteria
cases.steps: 1. Click the Advance Filter control
cases.expected: The panel exposes Upcoming/Active/Completed Work Order tiles, Active/Completed Inspection tiles, Task/Operation, Season, Farm, Start Date and End Date.

cases.title: Verify each work order status tile filters the map
cases.steps: 1. Select the Upcoming tile, then Active, then Completed, checking the map after each
cases.expected: Only plots matching the selected status remain highlighted after each selection.

cases.title: Verify the Start Date and End Date filters accept and apply a range
cases.steps:
1. Set a valid Start Date and End Date
2. Apply and observe the map
cases.expected: The date picker accepts the values, the map filters to work orders within the range. This has failed before with an unchangeable Jan-1900 default - confirm the fix.

cases.title: Verify an end date earlier than the start date is rejected
cases.steps: 1. Set End Date before Start Date and apply
cases.expected: A clear validation message is shown and no invalid filter is applied.

cases.title: Verify Reset clears all filter criteria
cases.steps:
1. Apply several criteria
2. Click Reset
cases.expected: All criteria are cleared and the map returns to the unfiltered default view.

cases.title: Verify combining status, operation and date criteria
cases.steps:
1. Select Active Work Orders + one operation + a date range
2. Apply
cases.expected: Only plots satisfying every criterion are highlighted; relaxing one criterion widens the result set predictably.

cases.title: Verify the sidebar renders the Farm > Field > Plot hierarchy
cases.steps:
1. Inspect the left sidebar
2. Expand a field node
cases.expected: The root shows the farm with field and plot counts; each field node shows number, acreage and its plots.

cases.title: Verify the sidebar search filters the tree
cases.steps: 1. Type a field number in the sidebar Search box
cases.expected: Only matching field/plot nodes remain; clearing the search restores the whole tree.

cases.title: Verify searching for a non-existent field
cases.steps: 1. Type a value that matches nothing (e.g. 'ZZZZ')
cases.expected: An empty/no-match state is shown, the app does not error and the search can be cleared.

cases.title: Verify selecting a field focuses it on the map
cases.steps: 1. Click a field node in the sidebar
cases.expected: The map pans/zooms to that field, the polygon is highlighted and the node is marked as selected.

cases.title: Verify field acreage is consistent across tree, map label and Details panel
cases.steps: 1. Note the acreage on the sidebar node, the map label and the Details aside for the same field
cases.expected: All three values are identical to two decimal places.

cases.prerequisite: A field selected on the map
cases.title: Verify the Details aside opens with Summary and Details tabs
cases.steps:
1. Click 'Details' on the aside panel
2. Switch between the Summary and Details tabs
cases.expected: The aside opens with farm/field information and both tabs render without errors.

cases.title: Verify plot-level information in the Details panel
cases.steps:
1. Select a field with one or more plots
2. Read the Details tab
cases.expected: Plot/project code, crop, variety, plot area and primary/secondary designation are shown and match the Planning module.

cases.title: Verify totals reconcile: sum of field acreage equals farm Total Area
cases.steps:
1. Capture each field acreage from the sidebar
2. Sum and compare with 'Total Area' on the Summary tab
cases.expected: The sum of individual field acreages equals the farm Total Area within the documented rounding tolerance.

cases.title: Verify site switch re-renders the map for the new site
cases.steps: 1. Switch Site while on Maps
cases.expected: The map re-centres on the new farm and the tree, counters and total area reload; no polygons from the previous site remain.

cases.title: Verify season switch updates plot and stage data on the map
cases.steps: 1. Switch Season and observe the tree and layer shading
cases.expected: Plot/project nodes and stage shading update to the selected crop year while season-independent geometry is unchanged.

cases.prerequisite: Maps open with a field selected
cases.title: Verify state after a browser refresh
cases.steps: 1. Select a field, then press F5
cases.expected: The app reloads to a valid Maps state without error; the selection is either restored or cleanly reset per design.

cases.expected: Both notes render in full with correct wrapping and no truncation.

cases.prerequisite: A work order created from a material template
cases.title: Verify material template data matches in the PDF
cases.steps: 1. Compare the PDF material section against the source material template
cases.expected: Every material, rate, unit and application value matches the template definition.

cases.prerequisite: A work order with weather logs
cases.title: Verify the weather table appears in the PDF
cases.steps: 1. Export a work order that has weather logs and inspect the PDF
cases.expected: The weather table is present with timestamp, temperature, wind speed and direction for each start and end event.

cases.prerequisite: A work order on the iOS app
cases.title: Verify PDF download from the mobile app
cases.steps: 1. Download the work order PDF from iOS and open it
cases.expected: The PDF downloads and opens correctly on the device with the same content as the web export.

cases.prerequisite: The same work order exported from web and iOS
cases.title: Verify web and mobile PDF exports are equivalent
cases.steps: 1. Export the same work order from both platforms and compare section by section
cases.expected: Both PDFs contain the same data and sections; any deliberate difference is documented.

cases.title: Verify attachments are not retrievable by unauthenticated URL
cases.steps: 1. Copy an attachment URL and open it in an unauthenticated session
cases.expected: Access is denied; the file is not served without a valid session and appropriate rights.

cases.prerequisite: A work order not yet started
cases.title: Verify the weather section exists before any job starts
cases.steps: 1. Open the work order detail on web and locate the weather section above the map
cases.expected: The section is present but shows no data, with a clear empty state rather than an error.

cases.prerequisite: A work order with started and ended jobs
cases.title: Verify weather data displays in tabular form
cases.steps: 1. Open the work order and inspect the weather section
cases.expected: A table shows Timestamp, Temperature, Wind Speed and Wind Direction for the start and end events of each plot.

cases.prerequisite: A work order with weather logs
cases.title: Verify weather details are included in the PDF export
cases.steps: 1. Download the work order PDF and inspect the weather table
cases.expected: The PDF contains the weather table with the same values as the web view.

cases.prerequisite: An inspection work order with jobs started and paused
cases.title: Verify weather logging applies to inspection work orders
cases.steps:
1. Start and pause jobs on plots of an inspection work order
2. Inspect the weather section
cases.expected: Weather is captured and displayed for inspection work orders exactly as for standard work orders.

cases.prerequisite: A completed job on a plot
cases.title: Verify the weather grid updates when spent hours are adjusted
cases.steps:
1. Note the weather log timestamp
2. Edit the spent hours / end time manually on web
3. Re-inspect the grid
cases.expected: The end date/time in the plot grid and the corresponding weather entry both update to the adjusted time. Known defect area - verify explicitly.

cases.title: Verify manual time adjustments are reflected in the PDF export
cases.steps: 1. Adjust spent hours, verify the updated weather log, then export the PDF
cases.expected: The PDF shows the updated weather grid with the adjusted timestamps. Known defect area - verify explicitly.

cases.prerequisite: A work order with multiple plots and alphanumeric field codes
cases.title: Verify sorting by field code then date/time
cases.steps: 1. Inspect the weather grid ordering across plots and dates
cases.expected: Records are sorted alphanumerically by field code and then chronologically by date and time within each code.

cases.title: Verify sorting is applied consistently in the PDF
cases.steps: 1. Generate the PDF and inspect the order of weather records
cases.expected: The sort order in the PDF matches the web UI exactly.

cases.prerequisite: A work order containing a plot with missing coordinates
cases.title: Verify weather grid exclusion for plots without coordinates
cases.steps:
1. Start and end the job on the plot lacking coordinates
2. Inspect the weather section and the plots map
cases.expected: The map section shows the 'no coordinates found' warning and the weather grid contains no record for that plot.

cases.prerequisite: A work order with multiple plots
cases.title: Verify plot-level weather data mapping on job start
cases.steps: 1. Start the job on each plot individually from the mobile app
cases.expected: The start date/time updates per plot and a weather entry is written against the correct plot ID.

cases.prerequisite: A job active on a plot
cases.title: Verify a weather log is written on partial pause
cases.steps: 1. Pause the job while the plot area is only partially complete
cases.expected: The end date/time updates immediately and a weather entry is added against the correct plot.

cases.title: Verify the weather log refreshes on plot completion
cases.steps: 1. Complete the area and pause the job again
cases.expected: The end date/time updates to the final time and the earlier partial-pause entry refreshes to the updated time and status.

cases.prerequisite: A job active on a plot
cases.title: Verify no weather log is written on Save Progress alone
cases.steps:
1. Start a job and only click Save Progress
2. Inspect the weather table
cases.expected: No weather entry is created for a save-only action. Known defect area - verify explicitly.

cases.title: Verify wind direction formatting
cases.steps: 1. Inspect the wind direction on a captured weather entry
cases.expected: The direction is displayed as a readable compass direction rather than a raw degree value or code.

cases.title: Verify weather behaviour when the device is offline
cases.steps:
1. Disable Wi-Fi and trigger a start or end job event
2. Open the weather section
cases.expected: The app remains stable and responsive, shows an offline indicator and does not hang waiting on the unreachable API.

cases.title: Verify no weather entry is created on Resume
cases.steps: 1. Start, pause and then resume a job
cases.expected: No new weather entry is created on resume; entries are only written on start, partial pause and completion.

cases.title: Verify rapid start/pause toggling does not duplicate logs
cases.steps: 1. Rapidly start and then pause within two seconds and inspect the weather table
cases.expected: The system records the events without duplicating entries or crashing the weather capture service.

cases.title: Verify weather capture on a multi-day work order
cases.steps: 1. Start a job just before midnight and pause it just after
cases.expected: The end date and time reflect the date change correctly and the weather log timestamps the actual moment of each action.

cases.prerequisite: Location permission set to 'While Using the App'
cases.title: Verify tracking logs for a normal shift
cases.steps:
1. Work a normal shift with the app in use
2. Open the location log from the app menu
cases.expected: Location points are recorded at the configured interval throughout the shift with plausible coordinates.

cases.prerequisite: Location permission set to 'While Using the App'
cases.title: Verify tracking logs across an overnight shift
cases.steps: 1. Work a shift that crosses midnight and inspect the log
cases.expected: Points are recorded continuously across the date boundary and are attributed to the correct shift.

cases.title: Verify supervisor tracking logs on a normal shift
cases.steps: 1. Work a shift as a supervisor and inspect the logs
cases.expected: The supervisor's own points are recorded and the supervisor can view logs for their team.

cases.title: Verify responsible tracking logs on a normal shift
cases.steps: 1. Work a shift as the responsible and inspect the logs
cases.expected: Points are recorded correctly and attributed to the responsible user.

cases.title: Verify offline tracking logs are captured and synced
cases.steps: 1. Work part of the shift offline, then reconnect
cases.expected: Points captured offline are stored locally and uploaded on reconnect with their original timestamps preserved.

cases.title: Verify logging while the app is in the foreground
cases.steps: 1. Keep the app in the foreground during a timed-in period and inspect the log
cases.expected: Points are recorded at the configured interval.

cases.title: Verify logging while the app is backgrounded
cases.steps: 1. Background the app during a timed-in period and inspect the log afterwards
cases.expected: Background logging follows the documented behaviour for the granted permission level, with no gaps beyond the expected interval.

cases.title: Verify logging stops when the app is killed
cases.steps:
1. Time in, then force-quit the app
2. Inspect the log for the period after the kill
cases.expected: No points are recorded after the app is killed, per the documented behaviour.

cases.title: Verify tracking with 'Allow Once' permission
cases.steps: 1. Grant 'Allow Once' and work briefly, then inspect the log
cases.expected: Points are recorded for the granted session and logging stops cleanly when the grant lapses.

cases.title: Verify behaviour when location permission is denied
cases.steps: 1. Deny location permission and attempt to use tracked features
cases.expected: The app clearly states that location access is required and blocks only the tracked features rather than crashing.

cases.title: Verify tracking logs from the Attendance screen
cases.steps: 1. Open the Attendance menu on web and click the tracking log icon for a user
cases.expected: The user's location log is displayed with timestamps and points matching the mobile capture.

cases.prerequisite: Tracking data on a planned work order
cases.title: Verify tracking logs from a planned work order
cases.steps: 1. Open a planned work order and click the tracking log icon
cases.expected: The log shows points captured while the user worked that work order.

cases.prerequisite: Tracking data on a general work order
cases.title: Verify tracking logs from a general work order
cases.steps: 1. Open a general work order and click the tracking log icon
cases.expected: The log displays correctly for the work order's timed-in users.

cases.prerequisite: Tracking data on an inspection work order
cases.title: Verify tracking logs from an inspection work order
cases.steps: 1. Open an inspection work order and click the tracking log icon
cases.expected: The log displays correctly for the inspection's timed-in users.

cases.title: Verify the shift filter on the tracking log
cases.steps: 1. Apply the shift filter and observe the plotted points
cases.expected: Only points from the selected shift are shown and the filter can be cleared.

cases.title: Verify the events filter on the tracking log
cases.steps: 1. Apply the events filter and observe the results
cases.expected: Only the selected event types are shown and the filter combines correctly with the shift filter.

cases.prerequisite: A user with a configured tracking interval
cases.title: Verify the configured interval is honoured in the captured data
cases.steps:
1. Set a 30-minute interval for a user
2. Have them work a shift and inspect the point spacing
cases.expected: Point spacing matches the configured interval within the documented tolerance.

cases.prerequisite: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari available
cases.title: Verify cross-browser rendering of the app shell and a data grid
cases.steps:
1. Open the app in each browser
2. Check the header, navigation, a data grid and a modal
cases.expected: Layout, fonts and interactions are consistent across all four browsers with no broken control or overlapping element.

cases.prerequisite: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari available
cases.title: Verify the core create-work-order flow in each browser
cases.steps: 1. Create and submit a work order in each browser
cases.expected: The flow completes successfully in every browser with identical results.

cases.title: Verify responsive behaviour at tablet widths
cases.steps:
1. Resize the browser to roughly 1024px and 768px
2. Inspect the header, sidebar, grids and the Create Work Order form
cases.expected: Content reflows without horizontal scrolling traps, controls remain reachable and no text is clipped.

cases.prerequisite: Records created on iOS and on web
cases.title: Verify data created on either platform is fully visible on the other
cases.steps:
1. Create a work order, an observation and a chat message on each platform
2. Verify each on the opposite platform
cases.expected: Every record is visible with complete data on the opposite platform after sync.

cases.title: Verify key pages load within the agreed threshold
cases.steps:
1. Measure first meaningful render for Maps, the Work Orders list, Harvest Central and Planning
2. Repeat three times and take the median
cases.expected: Each page renders within the agreed threshold and the measured values are recorded for trend tracking.

cases.title: Verify grid performance with a large record set
cases.steps: 1. Set the page size to 100 on the Work Orders list and page through the data
cases.expected: Paging, sorting and searching all respond within the agreed threshold with no browser freeze.

cases.title: Verify detail page load time scales with plot count
cases.steps: 1. Open the detail of each work order and record the load time
cases.expected: Load times remain within the agreed thresholds for each plot count with no timeout at 100 plots.

cases.prerequisite: A dashboard with 100 plots of live data
cases.title: Verify dashboard aggregation performance
cases.steps: 1. Load the dashboard for a 100-plot work order and observe aggregation and chart rendering
cases.expected: The dashboard loads within the agreed threshold, aggregations are accurate and charts render fully.

cases.prerequisite: Several users viewing the same work order
cases.title: Verify concurrent viewing of one work order
cases.steps: 1. Have five users open the same work order and refresh; have one make an update
cases.expected: All views load within the threshold, the update is visible to the others after refresh and no data inconsistency appears.

cases.title: Verify plot search and filter performance within a work order
cases.steps: 1. Search plots by name, filter by status and progress range, then combine filters
cases.expected: Each search and filter returns within the agreed threshold with accurate results.

cases.title: Verify horizontal privilege escalation is prevented
cases.steps:
1. As user A note a record ID belonging to grower B
2. As user A attempt to access it by URL and by direct API call
cases.expected: Both attempts are rejected server-side; no data belonging to another grower is returned.

cases.title: Verify vertical privilege escalation is prevented
cases.steps: 1. As a standard user invoke an admin-only endpoint directly
cases.expected: The request is rejected with an authorisation error and no admin action is performed.

cases.title: Verify input sanitisation against script injection
cases.steps:
1. Enter script and HTML markup into work order names, notes, chat messages and template names
2. View the stored values everywhere they render
cases.expected: Input is stored and rendered as literal text on every surface including PDFs and the mobile app; nothing executes.

cases.title: Verify resistance to SQL/query injection patterns
cases.steps: 1. Enter common injection payloads into search fields and submit
cases.expected: The application returns a normal empty or filtered result and never exposes a database error or unexpected data.

cases.title: Verify sensitive data is not exposed in URLs or logs
cases.steps: 1. Inspect URLs, browser storage and console output during a normal session
cases.expected: No credential, token or personal data is written to the URL, console or persistent browser storage in readable form.

cases.title: Verify local data is stored securely on the device
cases.steps: 1. Inspect the app's local storage after downloading work orders and capturing offline data
cases.expected: Cached business data is protected per the security policy and is unreadable without the app's credentials.

cases.title: Verify plot acreage is consistent across Maps, Planning and Work Orders
cases.steps: 1. Pick five plots and compare acreage in Maps, Planning and a work order
cases.expected: All three surfaces report identical acreage to two decimal places for every plot checked.

cases.title: Verify work order counts reconcile between list, Maps layers and Planning
cases.steps: 1. Count work orders per status in the list, on the Maps layers and on the Planning board for the same scope
cases.expected: The three counts agree for every status.

cases.prerequisite: Hours logged across mobile and web
cases.title: Verify hours reconcile between the mobile log, the work order and Planning
cases.steps: 1. Log hours on mobile, then compare the work order hour log and the Planning consumed hours
cases.expected: All three agree exactly. Hours logged versus hours consumed is a known mismatch area - verify explicitly.

cases.title: Verify ticket counts and weights reconcile with D365
cases.steps: 1. Compare Harvest Central ticket counts and weights against the corresponding D365 records
cases.expected: Counts and weights agree for every field/variety checked.

cases.title: Verify no previously fixed defect has regressed
cases.steps: 1. Re-execute the verification steps for every defect closed in the previous two releases
cases.expected: No closed defect reproduces; any that does is logged immediately with its original reference.

cases.title: Verify the end-to-end smoke path on web and iOS
cases.steps: 1. Execute login, map load, create work order, sync to mobile, start job, enter progress, end job, end work order and verify on web
cases.expected: The complete path succeeds on both platforms with no blocking error at any step.

cases.title: Verify the application version and environment after deployment
cases.steps: 1. Check the version and environment labels on web and iOS against the release record
cases.expected: Both match the intended build for the environment under test.

cases.title: Verify destructive actions require explicit confirmation
cases.steps: 1. Trigger delete on a work order, a ticket, an attachment and a template
cases.expected: Each presents a clear confirmation naming the record, and cancelling makes no change.

cases.title: Verify progress indication on long-running operations
cases.steps: 1. Trigger a large export, a bulk post and a large work order save
cases.expected: Each shows a progress or busy state, the UI is not silently frozen, and completion or failure is clearly reported.

cases.title: Verify validation messages are specific and actionable
cases.steps: 1. Trigger validation failures across the create forms in every module
cases.expected: Each message names the field and the problem in plain language; no raw error codes or stack traces are shown.

cases.title: Verify keyboard navigation through the primary flows
cases.steps: 1. Navigate the header, a data grid and the Create Work Order form using only the keyboard
cases.expected: All interactive elements are reachable and operable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator.

cases.title: Verify colour contrast on key surfaces
cases.steps: 1. Check text and control contrast on the header, grids, status chips and map legends
cases.expected: Contrast meets the agreed accessibility standard and status is never conveyed by colour alone.

cases.title: Verify recovery from a mid-session backend outage
cases.steps: 1. Take the backend offline mid-session, attempt several actions, then restore it
cases.expected: Failures are reported clearly, no data is silently lost, and the app recovers without requiring a re-login once the backend returns.

cases.prerequisite: A record edited simultaneously on two platforms
cases.title: Verify concurrent edit handling
cases.steps: 1. Edit the same work order on web and iOS at the same time and save both
cases.expected: The documented conflict rule is applied deterministically, the losing edit is reported to its author, and no data is corrupted.
